# Tunables

Every engine threshold, from the KDoc in `engine/src/commonMain/kotlin/pianoanchor/engine/Tunables.kt`.

| Name | Value | Meaning | Why | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CHORD_CLUSTER_MS` | 90 | Notes whose onsets fall within this many milliseconds of a cluster's first note form one chord. | a chord is one physical gesture, so the window is absolute (not tempo-scaled, not widened for beginners). | practice-mode scorers group chord tones within 50–90 ms; score-alignment research uses a tighter 35 ms simultaneity threshold (Nakamura et al., ISMIR 2017). 90 ms suits beginners. |
| `SYSEX_MAX_BYTES` | 65_536 | Largest System Exclusive payload (bytes between 0xF0 and 0xF7) the MIDI parser keeps; longer ones are discarded. | bounds memory if a device never sends 0xF7. | MIDI 1.0 sets no SysEx length limit; 64 KiB is far above any message the app reads (identity replies and parameter reads are tens of bytes). |
| `BLE_SCAN_TIMEOUT_MS` | 12_000 | How long a Bluetooth LE MIDI scan runs, in milliseconds, before it stops by itself. | a piano that is on and free advertises often, so a short scan finds it; stopping early saves battery. | a surveyed open-source BLE MIDI app scans for 12 s; revisit after the T8 soak test. |
| `BLE_RECONNECT_INITIAL_MS` | 1_000 | Wait before the first attempt to reopen a dropped Bluetooth LE MIDI device, in milliseconds; each further attempt waits twice as long, up to [BLE_RECONNECT_MAX_MS]. | a brief radio drop should recover quickly, without retrying in a tight loop. | initial guess; revisit after the T8 60-minute soak test. |
| `BLE_RECONNECT_MAX_MS` | 30_000 | Longest wait between attempts to reopen a dropped Bluetooth LE MIDI device, in milliseconds. | caps the backoff so a piano that comes back is found soon, without hammering the Bluetooth stack. | initial guess; revisit after the T8 soak test. |
| `BLE_RECONNECT_GIVE_UP_MS` | 300_000 | Total backoff waiting, in milliseconds, after which the adapter stops trying to reopen a dropped Bluetooth LE MIDI device: no attempt starts once the waits since the drop would add up to more than this (the time the attempts themselves take is not counted). | covers briefly walking away from the piano, then stops draining the battery. | initial guess; revisit after the T8 soak test. |
| `BLE_LISTED_TIMEOUT_MS` | 5_000 | How long, in milliseconds, a Bluetooth LE MIDI device that Android reports as opened may take to show up in the device list; if it doesn't, the open counts as failed and the handle is closed. | Android lists the device before it hands back the opened device, so this only bounds the rare case of a link that drops in between; without it `connect` could wait forever. | initial guess, far above the expected delay of one main-looper callback; revisit after the T8 test. |
| `MONITOR_LOG_LINES` | 50 | How many lines the note monitor keeps in its live log (newest first); older lines are dropped. | enough to read back the last phrase played, while bounding the work of redrawing the log. | UI choice agreed in the note-monitor grill (2026-11-11). |
| `MONITOR_RECORDING_MAX_MS` | 1_800_000 | Longest note-monitor recording, in milliseconds after its first event; recording stops there with a notice. | bounds memory (a few MB of messages at most) while a fixture session lasts minutes. | agreed in the note-monitor grill (2026-11-11). |
